issue: swéh₂dyos comparative read elatively 'very sweet' (lexicon gloss allows it)
bʰéwgt-kʷe switches subject (dogs -> wolf) with no pronoun; English supplies 'he'
h₂életes is PRS 2DU/3DU; English 'We feed him' needs 1PL h₂élomes

péḱu ne widmé is 1PL 'we do not know' but English 'I do not know' (person); also péḱu means 'livestock, cattle', not 'money', so the PIE says a herdsman does not know cattle (meaning and §5 character break)
ph₂tr̥bʰós is DAT/ABL.PL 'to/from fathers'; subject 'My father sang' needs NOM.SG ph₂tḗr
kʷíd sh₂l̥bʰós: sh₂l̥bʰós is DAT/ABL.PL of 'salt'; 'What is salt?' needs NOM.SG (séh₂ls / sḗh₂l)
h₁édte 2PL addressed to the household, after a singular 'friend' turn; acceptable
swéh₂dt is AOR 'became tasty'; English generic present 'becomes tasty' (gnomic aorist at best)
gʰósteyes n̥smé gʷm̥sḱónti: bare ACC pronoun as goal of 'come' ('to us'); a dative or a place noun is the expected construction
préḱsdʰi s-aorist imperative in -dʰi is Indo-Iranian-style; acceptable
h₁áyt is AOR 'gave'; English generic 'gives' (gnomic aorist)
pótn̥yeh₂su is LOC.PL 'among the ladies'; subject 'My wife is cooking' needs NOM.SG pótnih₂
